# Camouflare 2.0.0

> Draft for maintainer review. Remove this note before publishing the GitHub Release.

Camouflare 2.0.0 gives caller-supplied headers and `request.post` transports with
enforceable redirect boundaries, validates request cookies and proxies, hardens tokenless
local mode, and pins the bundled Camoufox archive to a reviewed SHA-256 manifest. The major
version reflects two behavior changes that existing clients can observe; see
[Upgrading](#upgrading).

## What changed

- A `request.get` with non-`User-Agent` `headers` (including `Referer`) is served by a
  bounded direct HTTP transport that removes those headers before any cross-origin
  redirect. It is supported only for stateless, proxyless requests without screenshots,
  and it returns the buffered HTTP response rather than a rendered page.
- `request.post` always uses the browser context request transport with automatic
  redirects disabled; the first response is returned and the request is never replayed.
  Failures after the POST was sent report `requestOutcomeUnknown: true`.
- Direct HTTP GET follows at most ten redirects under one deadline, returns non-2xx
  responses, imports received cookies into the browser context, and merges them into
  `solution.cookies`, which now also carry `expiry`.
- Request cookies are validated and normalized, with public-suffix, IP-literal,
  `Secure`, `SameSite=None`, and cookie-prefix rules applied on the direct HTTP path.
  Unknown browser-export fields are ignored.
- `proxy` accepts only `http`, `https`, `socks4`, `socks5`, and `socks5h` servers with
  SOCKS credential rules; `url`, `headers`, and `userAgent` reject control characters.
- Tokenless mode accepts only loopback peers and `Host` values, same-origin browser
  requests, and JSON `POST /v1` bodies. `camouflare.asgi:app` requires
  `CAMOUFLARE_API_TOKEN`.
- `sessions.create` beyond `MAX_SESSIONS` returns HTTP 503 `POOL_UNAVAILABLE` with
  `retryable: true`; a session whose context cannot open a page is evicted; popup pages
  are closed with their request.
- Browser pool startup is shared between concurrent callers, keeps launched browsers
  accounted for until registration, and caps live plus closing browser generations at
  twice `POOL_MAX_BROWSERS`.
- Challenge clearance polling keeps one second of `maxTimeout` in reserve so the error
  envelope can still be produced.
- `scripts/camoufox-artifacts.json` pins the Camoufox release tag and per-platform
  SHA-256 digests; the fetch script and the CI, nightly, and release workflows resolve
  only that tag and verify every download.

## Upgrading

- Clients that send `headers` other than `User-Agent` lose JavaScript rendering and
  browser challenge handling on `request.get`, and receive `INVALID_REQUEST` when they
  also name a session, proxy, or screenshot. Remove headers the target does not need or
  clear the challenge first with a header-less request.
- `request.post` no longer renders the response or handles browser challenges, and
  rejects `returnScreenshot`. Clear challenges with a `request.get` in a session, then
  POST in that session.
- Cookies with `;` or control characters in `value`, unknown `sameSite` spellings, or
  public-suffix domains are rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`.
- External ASGI servers importing `camouflare.asgi:app` must set `CAMOUFLARE_API_TOKEN`.
- Allow memory and PID headroom for up to another `POOL_MAX_BROWSERS` browser processes
  during a recycle.
- See the [2.0 upgrade guide](https://github.com/mehmetcansahin/camouflare/blob/v2.0.0/docs/upgrade-to-2.0.md)
  for the full list.

## Container image

The immutable release image is available for Linux `amd64` and `arm64`:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/mehmetcansahin/camouflare:2.0.0
```

See the
[changelog](https://github.com/mehmetcansahin/camouflare/blob/v2.0.0/CHANGELOG.md#200---2026-09-06)
for the complete entry and the
[deployment guide](https://github.com/mehmetcansahin/camouflare/blob/v2.0.0/docs/deployment.md)
for production constraints and rollback guidance.
